newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Asian bank to help Bangladesh fight urban poverty.
newsitem.headline: Asian bank to help Bangladesh fight urban poverty.

text.p: Urban planners from home and abroad began a two-day meeting on Monday in Dhaka to discuss a plan to fight growing poverty in the Bangladesh capital, officials said.

They said the Manila-based Asian Development Bank (ADB) had pledged to finance the proposed "urban poverty reduction project" aimed at bringing down the poverty level of Dhaka's poor, estimated to number about five million.
An ADB official told reporters on Sunday that the Bank might provide up to $40 million for the five-year project.
"The credit will be used for income generating activities for slum dwellers and training programmes for new skills," said ADB consltant Susanna Price, who led an expert survey on the city's poor.

Local Government Minister Zillur Rahman, who formally inaugurated the meeting, said his government was "politically committed to the welfare of the poor. The government is pursuing a policy of equitable growth," he said.
Bangladesh officials said the project would target primarily Dhaka's 1.7 million slum dwellers.

According to the survey, some five milion of the city's 9.3 million dwellers live below the poverty line. It also revealed that Dhaka's three million "hardcore" poor included an estimated 90,000 destitutes, many of them homeless.
The proposed project has earmarked about 60 million taka ($1.5 million) to build night-shelters for street sleepers, according to official figures.
